body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 8 models with a format search (of 279 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 22.2 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 5 of 7 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 66%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (token agreement 100% → 67%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's) and openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 43.3 → 48.4, higher is worse).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB), groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB), add output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.2 dB) and linear bias in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 36.5 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): mul outputs end furthest from full precision, facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 keeping only -0.8 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 0.4 dB), bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 1.3 dB), linear in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 1.6 dB), linear in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 7.6 dB), attention in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), gelu in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 9.6 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB) and attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 3254 (59%), fp8_e3m4 1401 (25%), fp8_e1m6 873 (16%), ufp8_e2m6 23 (0.41%), ufp8_e3m5 1 (0.02%); 0.43% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.4 dB) and upsample in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.9 dB).

body:
1 missing capability keep 30 operations in 2 models (of 6 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (30 operations in 2 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 30 operations in 2 models: 30 calls (1.17% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 and embedding in openai-community/gpt2. Cost today: 0 of 30 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 30 wait for one; 4 workarounds proposed, 1 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 441 of 756 tensors passed between kernels (58%) in 6 models: 279 for attention heads split or merged, 142 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 279 operations (279 calls, 11% of all calls; 100 G MACs, 4.21% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 72 and linear → add (other reshapes) 58; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and google/vit-base-patch16-224 (36).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 441 of 756 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 754 operations in 6 models (754 calls, 29% of all calls), most often silu (210), layernorm (176) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst 9.2 dB SQNR over 754 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 32.5, most 82 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 82 planned groups), over 6 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 754 operations limited by the LUT and up to 82 kernel launches per pass

body: The surveyed IPU findings show the largest measured accuracy cost is quantization: with NX8's 8-bit formats, model outputs drop to a median 22.2 dB SQNR (worst 12.8 dB), 5 of 7 models with a prediction metric lose some of it (worst: token agreement 100% → 66% on the SD v1.5 VAE), and the tensors losing most in their best formats are layernorm/add/mul outputs in DiT-XL-2-256 (down to 32.1 dB), while accumulated path error is worst for mul outputs (−0.8 dB in DiT). The most costly structural limitation is run-time addressing, which blocks 30 embedding operations in 2 models from running directly (data movement only, no MACs) and currently has no working workaround. Next, layout conversions affect 441 of 755 inter-kernel tensors (58%), mostly for attention-head split/merge (279), forcing the reading kernel to rearrange data across 279 calls (11% of calls, 4.2% of MACs). Resource limits follow: 754 operations (29% of calls) must use a 256-entry LUT with worst 9.2 dB SQNR, and forward passes need a median 32.5 kernel launches (up to 81). Compute efficiency (MAC utilisation) and instruction-memory use are not yet measured, and no extra kernels have been required so far for workarounds.
title: GLM summary

body: **Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip)** would put 30 operations in 2 models on the chip directly, with no workaround: 30 calls (1.17% of all calls) and no MACs (they only move data); the accuracy it would recover is not measured yet (no workaround evaluated).
